annotationRationale: Recognizing the incircle connects the spatial configuration to the area-inradius relation. Isosceles symmetry supplies the altitude, and perpendicularity permits the final Pythagorean calculation.
sourceMethod: Followed the official isosceles-altitude, area-inradius, and right-triangle method. Introduced a separate tangency point T to explain the spatial construction explicitly.

review.mathCheck: Tangency to the three side segments makes the sphere's planar section the incircle. The altitude is √(225−144)=9, area is 108, and semiperimeter is 27, giving r=4. Thus the center-to-plane distance is √(36−16)=2√5, choice D.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, originally worded adaptation of MAA solution 21 on page 12 and its figure. Using a named contact point T instead of D preserves the official altitude, inradius, and spatial right-triangle method.
review.annotationCheck: The area-inradius identity and final perpendicularity are explained sufficiently for AMC 10. The selected assessed and supporting nodes fit; neither Heron's formula nor an alternative spatial method is needed.
